requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: createrepo_c was used to build repo metadata in /srv/localrepo from downloaded RPMs, and a systemd-managed python3 http.server bound to the node's own IP on port 8080 served it; repomd.xml returned HTTP 200 both before and after restart.

The two enabled Red Hat CDN repos were disabled via dnf config-manager and cdn.redhat.com was blackholed in /etc/hosts; curl to cdn.redhat.com and dnf makecache against the remote repo both failed to connect, directly proving unreachability rather than merely configuring it.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remote repositories are unreachable
requirements.summary: With only local-repo enabled and remote repos proven unreachable in the same command, dnf install of tree completed with the transaction table showing Repository: local-repo, and rpm -q confirmed installation.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — building and serving a local repo from local storage, making the usual remote repositories genuinely unreachable, and installing a package from the local repo under that condition — are directly and coherently evidenced by command output on node1. The executor additionally ran the node-restart evidence protocol: it captured a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id, active service, installed package, blocked remote), issued an acknowledged reboot, observed connection disruption followed by a new boot_id, and confirmed full recovery of the local repo service, installed package, and blocked-remote state post-restart, consistent with the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. This restart evidence exceeds what the task itself required but is high quality and does not surface any regression.
limitations: The first HTTP-server start attempt (cmd-82b012cec1264bd0) was cut off mid-script with return_code 143; the trace cannot fully establish whether an orphaned python3 process briefly existed before the systemd unit took over the port, though final state shows no conflict.

The 'dnf repoquery --installed' output showed reponame '@System' for tree, which is expected/normal dnf behavior for already-installed packages and does not contradict the install-time transaction table showing 'local-repo' as the source.

operational_hygiene.summary: The first attempt to start the repo HTTP server (cmd-82b012cec1264bd0) used an ad hoc nohup'd python3 process with a pid file under /var/run and was terminated mid-script (return_code 143), likely from a command timeout; this was a bounded, low-risk troubleshooting step that was superseded by a cleaner systemd-unit approach in cmd-20e3322c24c84c44, and post-executor listening-socket evidence shows only a single python3 process bound to port 8080 with no port conflicts or failed units, so no persistent residue resulted. A backup file /etc/hosts.bak was created before editing /etc/hosts (cmd-82b012cec1264bd0/cmd-1d4a1a371de64fb8) and left in place; this is a reasonable safety artifact rather than unwanted residue. The after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows zero failed services and a clean listening-socket diff (only the intended new sshd/chronyd PIDs from the reboot and the new local-repo-httpd socket), confirming no lasting damage from the earlier aborted attempt.
